_schema_notes: Each question has: id, category, difficulty (easy|medium|hard), prompt, choices (array of 4 strings), answer (0-3 index into choices).
Optional: quip_correct, quip_wrong — shown in the modal after answering. If absent, the game falls back to generic quips.
Scoring multipliers by difficulty: easy 1.5x, medium 2.0x, hard 3.0x. Configurable in Scoring.h.
The 'meta' category is for questions about the game itself — rules, mechanics, what a stone block does. These are always fair game.
Add as many questions as you like. The loader shuffles at startup and tracks what's been asked this session so repeats are rare.

questions.prompt: Which series uses the Dallara IR-18 as its spec chassis?
questions.quip_wrong: That's a stone for your trouble.

questions.prompt: What year did the first Indianapolis 500 take place?
questions.quip_correct: Ray Harroun won it in a Marmon Wasp.
questions.quip_wrong: May 30, 1911 — mark it down.

questions.prompt: In Formula 1, how many drivers share the front row of the starting grid?
questions.quip_correct: Pole and P2, side by side.
questions.quip_wrong: It's just two — pole and P2.

questions.prompt: How many laps make up the Indianapolis 500?
questions.quip_wrong: 200 laps around the 2.5-mile oval.

questions.prompt: What does DRS stand for in Formula 1?

questions.quip_wrong: Drag Reduction System — opens the rear wing to cut drag.

questions.prompt: Who was the last driver to win the Formula 1 World Championship for Ferrari?
questions.quip_wrong: Kimi Räikkönen, 2007 — the Iceman cometh.

questions.prompt: Who holds the all-time record for most Formula 1 pole positions?
questions.quip_wrong: Lewis Hamilton — 104 poles as of 2024.

questions.prompt: In rallying, what does the term 'pacenote' refer to?

A penalty added to a driver's stage time
The target lap time set by the event organizer
A fine issued for exceeding service park speed limits
